discovered.detail: Hantaan virus identified by Lee Ho-wang (Korea) in 1976 from striped field mice near the Hantan River; isolated 1978, named 1980. Sin Nombre virus (HPS) identified 1993 in the US Four Corners outbreak.
discovered.source_name: Korea Herald profile of Lee Ho-wang

earliest_evidence.detail: Chinese medical writings ~AD 960 may describe HFRS; first well-documented in Manchuria (1930s) and among ~3,000 UN troops in the Korean War.
earliest_evidence.source_name: general history (not verified online this session)

vaccine.detail: Hantavax (inactivated Hantaan vaccine) developed 1988, marketed in South Korea 1990; China has its own HFRS vaccines. No vaccine for HPS.

viruses.status_2026: China still reports thousands of HFRS cases a year (CFR ~0.3-1%); HPS sporadic in the Americas (Andes virus person-to-person). Gene Hackman's wife Betsy Arakawa died of HPS in Feb 2025 (verify).
fun_fact: Hantaan virus is named after Korea's Hantan River, where its rodent host was caught.
viruses.image_hint: CDC PHIL: search 'Sin Nombre virus' TEM (Cynthia Goldsmith); specific ID not verified
viruses.notes: Best cumulative: China 1950-2007 46,427 reported HFRS deaths (CFR peaked 14.2% in 1969). Korean War: ~3,000-3,200 UN cases, CFR ~5-15% - no published death count found (estimated low hundreds; do not compute). Global annual death estimate not available (GBD does not model hantavirus). Puumala vs Hantaan cause of Korean War cases debated (History.com 2026). China HFRS in 1950s-80s: China figure covers it; 1980s peak (~100k+ cases/yr) not separately retrieved.
